import numpy as np

# The feature vector x, written out. phi in weights.npy holds one parameter
# per entry, in this order: the bias, then NUMERIC, then ONEHOT.

# Numeric columns, used as they are.
NUMERIC = ["age", "Medu", "Fedu", "traveltime", "studytime", "failures",
           "famrel", "freetime", "goout", "Dalc", "Walc", "health", "absences"]

# Categorical columns: each (column, level) is a feature that is 1 when the
# column equals that level and 0 otherwise. One level per column is left out
# (it is absorbed by the bias), so a binary column contributes one feature.
ONEHOT = [
    ("school", "MS"), ("sex", "M"), ("address", "U"), ("famsize", "LE3"),
    ("Pstatus", "T"),
    ("Mjob", "health"), ("Mjob", "other"), ("Mjob", "services"), ("Mjob", "teacher"),
    ("Fjob", "health"), ("Fjob", "other"), ("Fjob", "services"), ("Fjob", "teacher"),
    ("reason", "home"), ("reason", "other"), ("reason", "reputation"),
    ("guardian", "mother"), ("guardian", "other"),
    ("schoolsup", "yes"), ("famsup", "yes"), ("paid", "yes"), ("activities", "yes"),
    ("nursery", "yes"), ("higher", "yes"), ("internet", "yes"), ("romantic", "yes"),
]

phi = np.load("weights.npy")


def features(student):
    x = [1.0]
    x += [float(student[c]) for c in NUMERIC]
    x += [float(student[c] == level) for c, level in ONEHOT]
    return np.array(x)


def grade_model(student):
    return float(phi @ features(student))
